Once the Chief Mufti of a breakaway Chechen republic during the First Chechen War, this politician later switched allegiance to Moscow and became president of the Chechen Republic before being assassinated by a bomb at a 2004 Victory Day parade — who is he?

Akhmad Kadyrov (23 August 1951 - 9 May 2004) was a Russian politician and revolutionary who served as Chief Mufti of the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria in the 1990s during and after the First Chechen War.
Recognized as monarch while still a boy living in Switzerland, this king of Siam returned home in 1945 only to die under mysterious circumstances the following year — who was he?
Ananda Mahidol (20 September 1925 - 9 June 1946) was the eighth king of Siam (later Thailand) from the Chakri dynasty, titled Rama VIII.
Before he became the first governor of New South Wales, this British naval officer started out as an apprentice on a whaling ship and even spent time seconded to the Portuguese Navy — who was he?
Arthur Phillip (11 October 1738 - 31 August 1814) was a British Royal Navy officer who served as the first governor of the Colony of New South Wales.

Fought on September 19, 1356, during the Hundred Years' War, this clash saw Edward the Black Prince and 6,000 Anglo-Gascons defend a fortified position against 14,000 to 16,000 French attackers. Name it.
Battle of Poitiers was fought on 19 September 1356, during the Hundred Years' War, between a French army commanded by King John II and an Anglo-Gascon force under Edward, the Black Prince.
This French politician left a center-right party in 2017 to join Emmanuel Macron's new movement, then served as France's economy and finance minister from 2017 to 2024 — who is he?
Prince Frederick, Duke of York and Albany

Chin Peng (21 October 1924 - 16 September 2013), born Ong Boon Hua, was a Malayan communist politician, guerrilla leader, and revolutionary.

While working for the RAND Corporation, this military analyst leaked a top-secret Pentagon study on Vietnam War decision-making to major newspapers in 1971, later facing Espionage Act charges carrying up to 115 years — who is he?
Daniel Ellsberg (April 7, 1931 - June 16, 2023) was an American political activist, economist, and United States military analyst.
A former governor of California, he led the Supreme Court through Brown v. Board, Miranda, and Loving — and chaired the commission that probed JFK's assassination. Which chief justice?

Earl Warren (March 19, 1891 - July 9, 1974) was an American attorney and politician who served as the 30th governor of California from 1943 to 1953, and as the 14th chief justice of the United States from 1953 to 1969.
Manufactured by Airbus Helicopters under the designation EC665, this four-blade attack helicopter first entered service in 2003 — which aircraft?
Eurocopter Tiger is a four-blade, twin-engine attack helicopter which first entered service in 2003.

Fusako Shigenobu (born September 28, 1945) is a Japanese communist activist, writer, and the founder and leader of the now-disbanded militant group Japanese Red Army (JRA).

Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia

Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia
In Norse mythology, this female being presides over an underworld realm that shares her name, receiving a portion of the dead — who is she?
Hel (mythological being) (Old Norse) is a female being in Norse mythology who is said to preside over an underworld realm of the same name, where she receives a portion of the dead.
After earning a law doctorate from Cornell, which Taiwanese politician led the Legislative Yuan caucus for the Taiwan People's Party from 2024?
Huang Kuo-chang (pinyin: Hung Guchng; Peh-e-j: Ng Kok-chhiong; born (1973-08-19)19 August 1973) is a Taiwanese legal scholar and politician.

J. E. B. Stuart (February 6, 1833 - May 12, 1864) was a Confederate cavalry general during the American Civil War.
This biblical queen, wife of King Ahab of Israel, was thrown from a window on the orders of Jehu and devoured by dogs, as the prophet Elijah had foretold — who was she?
Jezebel was the daughter of Ithobaal I of Tyre and the wife of Ahab, King of Israel, according to the Book of Kings of the Hebrew Bible (1 Kings 16).
This member of the First Triumvirate led the Gallic Wars, defeated Pompey, and sparked the political chaos that would end the Republic. Who?

Julius Caesar (12 or 13 July 100 BC - 15 March 44 BC) was a Roman general, statesman, and author who was the dictator of the Roman Republic almost continuously from 49 BC until his assassination in 44 BC.
Though named for one region, this Hohenzollern realm was actually based in the Margraviate of Brandenburg and rose from the work of 'The Great Elector.' What was it?
Kingdom of Prussia was a German state that existed from 1701 to 1918.
Born in Karnal to a wealthy Rajput family, this lawyer became the first prime minister of his newly founded nation and, revered as 'Leader of the Nation,' was assassinated in 1951 — who was he?
Liaquat Ali Khan (1 October 1895 - 16 October 1951) was a Pakistani lawyer, politician and statesman who served as the first prime minister of Pakistan from 1947 until his assassination in 1951.

Serving as the third and last Commonwealth president for barely five weeks in 1946, this man then became the first leader of the newly independent Philippine republic before dying in office in 1948 — who was he?
Manuel Roxas (January 1, 1892 - April 15, 1948) was the fifth president of the Philippines, serving from 1946 until his death in 1948.
Described in Genesis as the king of Salem and a priest of 'God Most High,' this biblical figure blesses Abram with bread and wine and is later invoked in the Epistle to the Hebrews — who is he?
Melchizedek was the king of Salem and priest of El Elyon (often translated as "God Most High").
Serving as the sixth chief of a major right-wing Hindu nationalist organization since 2009, this Indian activist was born in 1950 — who is he?

Mohan Bhagwat (born 11 September 1950) is an Indian activist who is serving as the sixth and current Sarsanghchalak (Chief) of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a right-wing Hindutva paramilitary organisation, since 2009.
Founded in 2023 by Pieter Omtzigt, what is the name of this Christian-democratic political party in the Netherlands?
New Social Contract is a Christian-democratic political party in the Netherlands founded by Pieter Omtzigt in 2023.
This November 1942 Allied invasion of French North Africa, a three-pronged strike at Casablanca, Oran and beyond, gave U.S. forces their first foothold against the Axis — what was it called?
Operation Torch (8-16 November 1942) was an Allied invasion of French North Africa during World War II.
Succeeding his father's abdication in 2013, this monarch is the eldest child of King Albert II and married Mathilde d'Udekem d'Acoz, with whom he has four children — who is he?
Philippe of Belgium (born 15 April 1960) is King of the Belgians, and is the eldest child of King Albert II and Queen Paola.
The first person from Uttar Pradesh and the first member of the BJP to hold the office, this Indian lawyer and politician served as his country's president from 2017 to 2022. Who is he?
Ram Nath Kovind (born 1 October 1945) is an Indian politician and lawyer who served as the president of India from 2017 to 2022.
Born in British Hong Kong and once a Member of Parliament, this academic and broadcaster now co-directs a grand-strategy program at Yale and co-hosts the podcast 'The Rest Is Politics' — who is he?
Rory Stewart (born 3 January 1973) is a British academic, broadcaster, writer, and former diplomat and politician.
This Austrian politician first became a government minister overseeing refugee integration in 2011, then served two separate terms as chancellor — who is he?
Sebastian Kurz (born 27 August 1986) is an Austrian former politician who served twice as Chancellor of Austria, first from 2017 to 2019 and then again from 2020 to 2021.
Documented in some form across Buddhism, Christianity, Vodou, Hinduism, Islam, and more, this altered state is attributed to control of the body by ghosts, demons, or deities — what is it called?
Spirit possession is an altered state of consciousness and associated behaviors purportedly caused by the control of a human body and its functions by spirits, ghosts, demons, angels, or deities.

Sparked when riot police suppressed a student demonstration on International Students' Day, this eleven-day, entirely nonviolent transition of power in November 1989 ended 41 years of one-party Communist rule in Czechoslovakia — name this event?
Velvet Revolution was a non-violent transition of power in what was then Czechoslovakia, occurring from 17 November to 28 November 1989.
This British statesman began his political career as a Conservative MP for Newark but became the face of the Liberal Party, serving a record four non-consecutive terms as Prime Minister — who is he?
William Ewart Gladstone (29 December 1809 - 19 May 1898) was a British statesman who served four times as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
This Chinese statesman served as the first Premier of the People's Republic of China from 1949 until his death in 1976, doubling as foreign minister for the first nine years — who is he?

Zhou Enlai (pinyin: Zhu nli; Wade-; 5 March 1898 - 8 January 1976) was a Chinese statesman, diplomat, and revolutionary who served as the first Premier of the People's Republic of China from October 1949 until his death in January 1976.
Born Amir, this military commander was one of ten companions promised Paradise by the Prophet Muhammad and led a large section of the Rashidun Army before dying in the Plague of Amwas — who was he?
Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah: Companion of Muhammad and military leader (583–639)

Alaric I: King of the Visigoths from 395 to 410.

Allied invasion of Sicily: Part of World War 2 in 1943.

Angolan Civil War: 1975–2002 military conflict. The Angolan Civil War (Portuguese: Guerra Civil Angolana) was a civil war in Angola, beginning in 1975 and continuing, with interludes, until 2002.

A close aide to Egyptian presidents Nasser and Sadat, this official was allegedly a Mossad spy who fed Israel intelligence before the Yom Kippur War, then died mysteriously falling from a London balcony in 2007 — who was he?
Ashraf Marwan: Egyptian businessman and spy (1944–2007)

German invasion of Greece: World War II military campaign in 1941. The German invasion of Greece or Operation Marita (German: Unternehmen Marita), were the attacks on Greece by Italy and Germany during World War II.

Guion Bluford: First African-American in space (born 1942)
Son of Cnut the Great, this ruler was the last monarch of the North Sea Empire uniting England and Denmark before dying suddenly in 1042 — who was he?
Harthacnut: King of England (1040–42) and Denmark (1035–42)
After 28 years in Soviet state security and a long reign as Azerbaijan's Communist Party boss, this man rose to become his country's third president in 1993 — who was he?
Heydar Aliyev: President of Azerbaijan from 1993 to 2003.
Left for dead by his companions after a grizzly mauling on the Upper Missouri, this frontiersman's survival inspired the films Man in the Wilderness and The Revenant — who was he?
Hugh Glass: American fur trapper and frontiersman (1783–1833)

Iran–Iraq War: 1980–1988 armed conflict in West Asia.
Guided by 24 tirthankaras who conquered the cycle of rebirth, this Indian religion built its entire ethical code on strict nonviolence to all living things — which faith?
Jainism: Indian religion. The community supported networks of temples, libraries, and charitable institutions.
Expelled from the Labour Party in 2024 after standing as an independent, which British politician had earlier led that party and the Opposition from 2015 to 2020?
After an unsuccessful mission to Georgia and a life-changing 1738 conversion experience, this English cleric founded the revival movement that became known as Methodism — who was he?
Roman emperor from 527 to 565, his dream of restoring the empire saw his general Belisarius reclaim North Africa, Italy and Rome from the Ostrogoths — who was he?
Justinian I: Roman emperor from 527 to 565. The praetorian prefect Liberius reclaimed the south of the Iberian Peninsula, establishing the province of Spania.

This semi-nomadic Turkic people built a major trading empire from the 6th century CE, dominating the Volga-Don steppes, Crimea, and the Caucasus for roughly three centuries as a crossroads on the Silk Road?
Khazars: Historical semi-nomadic Turkic ethnic group.
The son of a former Greek prime minister himself, who has led Greece's centre-right governing party since 2016 and served as PM since 2019?
Kyriakos Mitsotakis: Prime Minister of Greece (2019–2023; since 2023). Mitsotakis has been president of the New Democracy party since 2016.
Raised by Zhou Enlai after his revolutionary father was executed, this politician served as China's premier from 1987 to 1998 — who is it?
Li Peng: Premier of China from 1987 to 1998. For much of the 1990s Li was ranked second in the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) hierarchy behind then CCP General Secretary Jiang Zemin.
This American activist began on the far left, swung to the far right in the 1970s, ran for president again and again, and founded a movement often likened to a cult — who is he?
After narrowly losing a disputed 2014 mayoral race that went to the European Court of Human Rights, this lawyer-turned-politician finally became mayor of Turkey's capital in 2019 — who is he?

Honored in Gnostic texts as the 'apostle to the apostles,' this follower of Jesus witnessed both his crucifixion and resurrection — who was she?

This retired U.S. Army lieutenant general served just 22 days as national security advisor before resigning over reports he misled officials about talks with Russia's ambassador — who is he?
Michael Flynn: U.S. Army general and former U.S. National Security Advisor (born 1958)

This Iranian Revolutionary Guard commander led the Muslim Peshmerga during the Iran–Iraq War and played a major role in restoring Iranian control over Kurdish territory before his death in 1983. Who was he?

N. Chandrababu Naidu: 13th Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh (born 1950)
The first Indian American to serve in a presidential cabinet, this politician was South Carolina's governor and then the UN ambassador under Donald Trump. Who is she?
Nikki Haley: American politician and diplomat (born 1972)

Omar al-Bashir: President of Sudan from 1989 to 2019.
He left school at 14 yet became Australia's 24th prime minister, having first served as treasurer under Bob Hawke before taking the top job in 1991 — who is he?
Paul Keating: Prime Minister of Australia from 1991 to 1996.
India's longest-serving Minister of Commerce and Industry, this politician also won the 2018 Carnot Prize for his work in energy policy — who is he?

A native of Zanzibar, she became Tanzania's first woman president in 2021 after ascending from the vice-presidency on her predecessor's death. Who is she?

Siddaramaiah: Chief Minister of Karnataka from 2013 to 2018 and 2023 to 2026.

Elected king of Poland in 1764 with the backing of Catherine the Great — with whom he'd become intimately involved at the Russian court — he became the last monarch of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; who was he?
Stanisław August Poniatowski: Ruler of Poland–Lithuania from 1764 to 1795.

Ceded by the Qing dynasty after its defeat in an 1895 war with a rising East Asian empire, this island served as that empire's first colony, governed for the next 50 years from a capital called Taihoku — what period of history is this?

Commander of the Indonesian Armed Forces during the country's 1998 transition from authoritarian rule, this retired general later chaired the Presidential Advisory Council — who is it?
Wiranto: Indonesian general and politician. On 27 July 2016, Wiranto was appointed Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal, and Security Affairs, replacing Luhut Binsar Panjaitan.
Dismembered by the Titans and reborn, this figure from Greek myth was sometimes identified with an Orphic version of Dionysus and linked by Aeschylus to Hades — who is he?
Zagreus: Figure in Greek mythology. In the earliest mention of Zagreus, he is paired with Gaia and called the "highest" god, though perhaps only in reference to the gods of the underworld.

Which of these is a physicist?
John Logie Baird is a physicist. In 1928, the Baird Television Development Company achieved the first transatlantic television transmission.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
What is the atomic number of Nihonium?
Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.
What is the atomic number of Strontium?
Strontium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sr and atomic number 38.
In what year did Edward Teller die?
Edward Teller: Born in Austria-Hungary in 1908, Teller emigrated to the US in the 1930s, one of the many so-called "Martians", a group of Hungarian scientist émigrés.
In what year was Oxygen discovered?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
Potassium chloride: Pfizer. Potassium chloride (KCl, or potassium salt) is a metal halide salt composed of potassium and chlorine.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet E2 family based?
Embraer E-Jet E2 family: Brazil. The Embraer E-Jet E2 family is a series of four-abreast narrow-body regional jet airliners designed and produced by the Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer.
Who is credited with discovering Molybdenum?
Molybdenum: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.
Who is credited with discovering Serotonin?
Serotonin: Arda Green. It is involved in mood, cognition, reward, learning, memory, and physiological processes such as vomiting and vasoconstriction.
Who is credited with discovering Beryllium?
Beryllium: Louis Nicolas Vauquelin. Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
Stretching from the thoracic diaphragm to the pelvic brim, this body region sits between the chest and the pelvis — which body part?
Abdomen (also belly or stomach in vertebrates, or metasoma in arthropods) is the front part of the torso between the thorax (chest) and pelvis in humans and in other vertebrates.
This English academic and broadcaster, an anatomist and archaeologist by training, was president of the charity Humanists UK from 2019 to 2022 — who is she?
Alice Roberts (born 19 May 1973) is an English academic, anatomist, archaeologist, TV presenter and author.
This symptom, not a diagnosis by itself, refers to a loss of appetite in humans and — under the name 'inappetence' — in animals from dogs to goats. Which symptom?
Anorexia (symptom) is a medical term for a loss of appetite.
Doctors reach for this NSAID not just for aches but to treat Kawasaki disease and rheumatic fever — and it's famous for its blood-thinning effect on platelets. What is it?
Aspirin is the genericized trademark for acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to reduce pain, fever, and inflammation, and as an antithrombotic.
Designed to replace the aging Tu-126 'Moss,' this Soviet early-warning aircraft saw only about 42 built before the USSR's breakup ended production in 1992 — what is it?
Beriev A-50 (NATO reporting name: Mainstay) is a Soviet-origin airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft that is based on the Ilyushin Il-76 transport plane.
Caused by a toxin that thrives in low-oxygen conditions — the same one sold cosmetically as 'botox' — this rare illness brings blurred vision and creeping paralysis but rarely a fever. What is it?
Botulism is a rare and potentially fatal illness caused by botulinum toxin (commonly referred to as botox), which is produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum.

First synthesized in 1950 by bombarding curium with helium-4 ions, this synthetic actinide element carries atomic number 98, symbol Cf, and the second-highest atomic mass of any element — which element?
Californium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cf and atomic number 98.
Discovered in 1801 by Giuseppe Piazzi and initially hailed as a new planet, this object in the main asteroid belt is now the only recognized dwarf planet orbiting within Neptune's path — what is it?
Ceres (dwarf planet) is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Marked by a stopped heartbeat and halted breathing, this reversible-sounding medical state was given its name once CPR and defibrillation made post-arrest resuscitation possible — what's it called?
Clinical death is the medical term for cessation of blood circulation and breathing, the two criteria necessary to sustain the lives of human beings and of many other organisms.
What's the statistical term for the extent to which two variables are linearly related — famously not the same thing as causation?
Correlation is a type of statistical relationship between two random variables or bivariate data.
Specialists in this branch of medicine handle skin infections, cancers, hair loss, and cosmetic concerns, sometimes even life-threatening conditions like severe burns — which medical field?
Dermatology is the branch of medicine dealing with the skin.
Partly blinded in a childhood fishing accident, this Alabama-born naturalist turned to insects, co-developed the theory of island biogeography, and founded the field of sociobiology. Who is he?
E. O. Wilson (June 10, 1929 - December 26, 2021) was an American biologist, naturalist, ecologist, and entomologist who developed the field of sociobiology.
Comprising around 50 species mostly found in the tropics, this fungal genus infects rye, wheat, barley, and other grasses, producing toxic alkaloids — name the group of fungi?
Ergot is a group of fungi of the genus Claviceps. The most prominent member of this group is Claviceps purpurea (rye ergot fungus).
This plant genus of roughly 850 species includes woody trees, vines, and epiphytes native to the tropics, though only two species are widely cultivated for their sweet fruit — what genus is it?
Ficus (or) is a genus of about 850 species of woody trees, shrubs, vines, epiphytes and hemiepiphytes in the family Moraceae.
This scholarly discipline covers the link between food and culture, from recipes and regional cooking styles to the rigorous science of good eating — what's it called?

Gastronomy is the study of the relationship between food and culture, the art of preparing and serving rich or delicate and appetizing food, the cooking styles of particular regions, and the science of good eating.
Flown by both the U.S. Navy and Britain's Royal Navy under the name Martlet, this 1940 carrier fighter went toe-to-toe with the Mitsubishi Zero over the Pacific — which aircraft?
Grumman F4F Wildcat is an American carrier-based fighter aircraft that entered service in 1940 with the United States Navy and the British Royal Navy.

Named from the Greek for 'different wings' because most species have forewings that are part membrane, part hardened shell, this group of 40,000 insect species is the one most consistently called 'true bugs' — name this insect group?
Heteroptera are a group of about 40,000 species of insects in the order Hemiptera.
Marked by shivering and confusion in mild cases and hallucinations or paradoxical undressing in severe cases, this condition is defined as a body core temperature below 35°C (95°F) — name it?
Hypothermia is defined as a body core temperature below 35.0 C (95.0 F) in humans.

Once found as far north as Texas's Lower Rio Grande Valley but now extirpated from the US, this slender wild cat comes in gray and red color morphs, ranging from Mexico to Argentina — what animal is it?
Jaguarundi (Herpailurus yagouaroundi); or is a wild cat native to the Americas.
Endemic to New Caledonia's mountain forests, this bluish-grey, nearly flightless bird sports bright red legs and unique nasal corns shared by no other bird — what is it?
Kagu (Rhynochetos jubatus) is a crested, long-legged, and bluish-grey bird endemic to the dense mountain forests of New Caledonia.
Caused by a specific type of waterborne bacteria, this form of atypical pneumonia brings cough, fever, muscle pain, and headache within days of exposure — what's it called?
Legionnaires' disease is a form of atypical pneumonia caused by any species of Legionella bacteria, quite often Legionella pneumophila.
Named for antennae often longer than its own body, this insect family boasts over 35,000 species and gets its name from a Greek myth about a shepherd transformed after angering nymphs — which group?
Longhorn beetle (Cerambycidae), also known as long-horned or longicorns (whose larvae are often referred to as roundheaded borers), are a large family of beetles, with over 35,000 species described.
This computer scientist led the on-board flight software for NASA's Apollo Guidance Computer and is credited with coining the very term 'software engineering' — who is she?
Margaret Hamilton (software engineer) (ne Heafield; born August 17, 1936) is an American computer scientist.
This hedge fund manager and licensed physician was among the first to predict and profit from the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis, later portrayed on screen in The Big Short. Who is he?
Michael Burry (born June 19, 1971) is an American investor, hedge fund manager, and licensed physician.
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this contractile tissue comes in skeletal, cardiac, and smooth forms and relies on the proteins actin and myosin to generate movement — name the tissue?
Muscle is a specialised soft tissue, one of the four basic types of animal tissues.
Once confused with its chemical twin tantalum, this element with atomic number 41 resists corrosion so well it's used in earrings for people allergic to nickel — which element?
Niobium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nb (formerly columbium, Cb) and atomic number 41.
Known for causing bones that fracture easily, this group of genetic disorders can also produce blue-tinted eye whites, short stature, and hearing loss. Name the condition?
Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), colloquially known as brittle bone disease, is a group of genetic disorders that all result in bones that break easily.
Favored by royalty in the Chinese Imperial court, this toy dog breed originated in China's ancient capital — name the breed?
Pekingese (also spelled Pekinese) is a breed of toy dog, originating in China.

A perennial legume native to the Eastern Hemisphere, this crop is a staple across the Indian Subcontinent, Africa and the Caribbean despite a name that sounds more like a bird than a bean. What is it?
Pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) is a perennial legume from the family Fabaceae native to the Eastern Hemisphere.

Native to North American grasslands, these burrowing, herbivorous ground squirrels come in five species, black-tailed, white-tailed, Gunnison's, Utah, and Mexican. Name this genus, Cynomys, by its common two-word name?
Prairie dog (genus Cynomys) are herbivorous burrowing ground squirrels native to the grasslands of North America.

This small herbivore belongs to the family Leporidae alongside hares, and the European species of its genus has been introduced to every continent except Antarctica — what bouncy little prey animal is it?
Rabbit are small mammals in the family Leporidae (which also includes the hares), which is in the order Lagomorpha (which also includes pikas).

Nicknamed 'Il Professore' for his academic background, this Italian politician served as European Commission President from 1999 to 2004 and was twice his country's prime minister, first after leading The Olive Tree coalition to victory — who is he?

Romano Prodi (born 9 August 1939) is an Italian politician who served as President of the European Commission from 1999 to 2004 and twice as Prime Minister of Italy, from 1996 to 1998, and again from 2006 to 2008.

These colorful predatory marine animals — single polyps usually anchored by their base — are named after a terrestrial flower and, unlike their jellyfish relatives, skip the medusa stage entirely; what are they?
Sea anemone (-) are a group of predatory marine invertebrate animals constituting the order Actiniaria.
Despite the name, this digestive organ is about 6.5 metres long; it's just narrower in diameter than its large counterpart. What organ is it?
Small intestine is an organ in the gastrointestinal tract where most of the absorption of nutrients from food takes place.
Known by his online username 'spez,' this web developer co-founded an airfare search engine before leading the world's seventh most-visited website as CEO — who is he?
Steve Huffman (born 1983 or 1984), also known by his Reddit username spez, is an American web developer and entrepreneur.
Born in 1946, this American serial killer often posed as an authority figure or feigned injury to lure young women to his car before assaulting and murdering them — who was he?
Ted Bundy (n Cowell; November 24, 1946 - January 24, 1989) was an American serial killer who kidnapped, raped and murdered dozens of young women and girls throughout 1974, 1975, and 1978.
A nasty complication of this inflamed-throat illness goes by the wonderfully old-fashioned name 'quinsy,' or peritonsillar abscess — what's the underlying condition?
Tonsillitis is inflammation of the tonsils in the upper part of the throat.
This phenolic aldehyde is the primary component of the vanilla bean's extract — and its synthetic version now flavors more foods than the natural one does. What is it?
Vanillin is an organic compound with the molecular formula C8H8O3.
Neither an insect nor a parasite despite its common name, this terrestrial crustacean is one of the few of its kind to have colonized dry land, likely since the late Paleozoic — what is it?
Woodlouse are terrestrial isopods in the suborder Oniscidea.
The simplest and smallest ketone, this colorless, pungent, highly flammable liquid mixes freely with water and lurks in nail polish remover and paint thinner — what is it?
Working at Baghdad's House of Wisdom around 820, this Islamic Golden Age scholar wrote a treatise whose Arabic title, Al-Jabr, gave us the very word "algebra." Who was he?
This Indian economist and philosopher won the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his work on welfare economics, and later received India's highest civilian honor — who is he?
Amartya Sen: Indian economist and Nobel laureate (born 1933)
Named from Greek words for 'curved' and 'vertebra,' this type of arthritis causes long-term inflammation where the spine meets the pelvis — what is it?
Ankylosing spondylitis: Type of arthritis of the spine. Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis from the disease spectrum of axial spondyloarthritis.
Known commonly as palms, this family of over 2,600 flowering plant species includes climbers, shrubs, and tree-like forms mostly found in the tropics — what's the family called?
Arecaceae: Palm family of flowering plants.
The famous AL 288-1 skeleton nicknamed 'Lucy,' unearthed in Ethiopia's Afar region, belongs to which extinct East African hominin species that lived roughly 3.9 to 2.9 million years ago?
Australopithecus afarensis: Extinct hominid from the Pliocene of East Africa.
Sharing its engine, transmission, and rotor system with the Huey utility helicopter, this rapidly-developed attack chopper became America's dedicated gunship escort in the Vietnam War — what is it?
Bell AH-1 Cobra: Family of attack helicopters.

A French child prodigy who wrote a treatise on conic sections at 16, then built one of the first mechanical calculators and traded letters with Fermat that helped birth probability theory — who was he?
Created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller, this esoteric programming language uses just eight simple commands and is often cited as a 'Turing tarpit' — what is it called?
Brainfuck: Esoteric, minimalist programming language. While Brainfuck is fully Turing-complete, it is not intended for practical use but to challenge and amuse programmers.
Its Latin name means "chisel-bearing," a nod to the stout egg-laying organs of its members — which insect suborder includes grasshoppers, ground-hoppers, and pygmy mole crickets?
Caelifera: Suborder of insects. The latter should not be confused with the mole crickets (Gryllotalpidae), which belong to the other Orthopteran suborder Ensifera.
A founder of humanistic psychology, this American psychologist pioneered person-centered therapy, an approach that also shaped student-centered learning in education — who is he?
Certified in 1984 and developed into a freighter variant for FedEx, this single-engine turboprop utility plane typically seats nine and can be fitted with floats or skis — which aircraft?
Cessna 208 Caravan: Family of utility transport aircraft.
Blooming in autumn and closely associated with the month of November, this East Asian flowering genus in the daisy family boasts thousands of horticultural varieties — which flower?
Chrysanthemum: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family.

Believed to be the first coffee species ever cultivated, this plant, native to the forests of Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Yemen, still accounts for roughly 60% of global coffee production — what's its scientific name?
Coffea arabica: Species of coffee plant. Coffea arabica, also known as the Arabica coffee, is a species of flowering plant in the coffee and madder family Rubiaceae.
Produced mainly by the adrenal cortex and surging in response to stress and low blood sugar, this steroid hormone is sold as medicine under the name hydrocortisone — what is it?
Built from microfilaments, intermediate filaments, and microtubules, this network gives a cell its shape and lets it contract and migrate — what is it?
Cytoskeleton: Network of filamentous proteins that forms the internal framework of cells.
Native to the Mediterranean and nicknamed 'clove pink' for a spicy fragrance reminiscent of cinnamon and nutmeg, what flower is this?
Dianthus caryophyllus: Species of flowering plant.
Element 105 sparked a long Cold War naming dispute, claimed first by a Soviet institute in 1968 and then by Berkeley in 1970 before being settled in 1993 — which synthetic element?
Dubnium: Chemical element with atomic number 105 (Db)
The first woman admitted to MIT, this environmental chemist was the first to apply chemistry to nutrition and founded the home economics movement — who was she?
Ellen Swallow Richards: American engineer and chemist (1843–1911)
The major female sex hormone, this estrogen drives the development of secondary sexual characteristics and helps maintain reproductive tissues from puberty through pregnancy — what is it?
Known for its smooth silvery-grey bark and toxin-laced but edible nuts, this deciduous tree native to Europe includes the striking copper-leaved cultivar among its ornamentals — which species?
Fagus sylvatica: Species of deciduous tree. It is native to much of Europe, growing in humid climates.
Lacking a body cavity and equipped with just one opening for both eating and excreting, these simple unsegmented invertebrates are named for their shape — what are they?
Found in the rainforests and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa, this snake has the longest fangs of any venomous species — up to two inches — and the highest venom yield of any snake — which snake?
Gaboon viper: Species of snake. It is the largest member of the genus Bitis.
The only venomous lizard native to the United States, this sluggish reptile from the Southwest rarely poses a real threat despite its fearsome reputation — what is it?
Gila monster: Largest species of lizard in the United States.

Despite its name, this marine reptile's shell ranges from olive to black — its nickname actually comes from the color of the fat beneath its carapace, built up from an all-plant diet — which species is this?
Green sea turtle: Species of large sea reptile. The dorsoventrally flattened body of C. mydas is covered by a large, teardrop-shaped carapace; it has a pair of large, paddle-like flippers.

Made by fusing heavy nuclei in tiny quantities, this superheavy element 108 has a special isotope whose "magic numbers" of protons and neutrons make its deformed nucleus unusually stable — what is it?
Hassium: Chemical element with atomic number 108 (Hs)
Its name means 'river horse' in Ancient Greek, yet this semiaquatic sub-Saharan giant — the largest even-toed ungulate alive — is more closely tied to pigs than to horses; what is it?
Hippopotamus: Species of large semi-aquatic mammal.
Marketed as Buscopan, this anticholinergic medication treats abdominal cramps, bladder and biliary spasms, and can ease respiratory secretions near the end of life — what drug is it?
Hyoscine butylbromide: Anticholinergic medication. It is also used to improve excessive respiratory secretions at the end of life.
Sitting on the electromagnetic spectrum between visible light and microwaves, this invisible radiation makes up most of the black-body glow given off by objects near room temperature — what is it?

Infrared: Form of electromagnetic radiation. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.

This Dutch microscopist showed that an insect's egg, larva, pupa, and adult are all one animal, pioneered the microscope in dissections, and in 1658 became the first to observe red blood cells — who was he?
Jan Swammerdam: Dutch biologist and microscopist (1637–1680)
Committed to accuracy and verification, this occupation and set of methods involves gathering and distributing the day's news — what field is it?
Journalism: Production of reports on current events.
Native to southern China and roughly the size of a large olive, which citrus fruit closely resembles a tiny orange and is famously cold-hardy?
Kumquat: Species of small fruit-bearing tree.
Often beginning in the bone marrow, this group of cancers floods the body with immature 'blast' cells, bringing easy bruising, bone pain, and frequent infections — what is it?
Marketed as Imodium, this opioid-class medication treats diarrhea without crossing the blood-brain barrier at normal doses?
Loperamide: Medicine used to reduce diarrhea.
Males of this widespread dabbling duck species sport iridescent green heads, while females have brown-speckled plumage — which bird?
Mallard: Species of duck. The mallard or wild duck (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.

Entering US Navy service in 1961 before the Marines and Air Force adopted it too, this twin-engine supersonic jet became America's most-produced supersonic military aircraft with 5,195 built — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II: Fighter aircraft family developed from 1958.
A physician-turned-hedge-fund-manager, this investor famously predicted the subprime mortgage crisis and was portrayed in the 2015 film The Big Short — who is he?
Michael Burry: American hedge fund manager (born 1971)
Born in Taiwan but naturalized in Japan, this businessman invented the world's first prepackaged instant noodle brand and later created Cup Noodles — who is he?
Momofuku Ando: Taiwanese-Japanese inventor and businessman (1910–2007)
Most often triggered by a viral infection and capable of progressing to heart failure or cardiac arrest, which condition involves inflammation of the heart muscle itself?

Myocarditis: Inflammation of the heart muscle. Myocarditis can progress to inflammatory cardiomyopathy when there is associated ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction due to chronic inflammation.
This Danish physicist won the 1922 Nobel Prize for a model of the atom in which electrons leap between discrete, stable orbits around the nucleus — who is he?
Native to East Africa and known in some places as 'lady's fingers,' this mallow-family plant is prized for its edible green (sometimes red) seed pods — what is it?
Prized both as a delicacy and, in some species, for the pearls grown within its shell, which salt-water bivalve is this?
Oyster: Variety of families of Mollusca.
Whose name comes from Greek words for 'congealed' and 'curdled' — this plant-cell-wall polymer is extracted from citrus as a powder that makes jams and jellies set?
Pectin: Structural carbohydrate in the cell walls of land plants and some algae.
This branch of linguistics studies how spoken languages organize meaningful sound units — the kind of contrast that separates 'bat' from 'gnat' — what field is it?
Phonology: Study of sound organization in languages.

Proposed in 1904 and finally proven a century later using Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow techniques, this problem asks whether any loop-shrinkable finite 3D space must be a hypersphere — which famous problem?
Poincaré conjecture: Theorem in geometric topology.
Also known as face blindness, this cognitive disorder leaves a person unable to recognize familiar faces — even their own — while other visual skills stay intact. What is it?
Prosopagnosia: Cognitive disorder of face perception. Prosopagnosia should not be confused with prosopometamorphopsia, a disorder characterized by altered perceptions of faces.
Some specimens of this native European tree, whose acorns dangle on long stalks, are believed to be over 1,000 years old — name the species?
Quercus robur: Species of flowering plant.
Striking children recovering from a viral illness like the flu, this brain disease has been linked in about 90% of cases to aspirin use — what is it called?
Reye syndrome: Rapidly worsening brain disease.
Also called baked-apple berry or Arctic berry, this amber-hued fruit resembling a blackberry grows wild across boreal forests and Arctic tundra — what's its scientific name?
Rubus chamaemorus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
Nicknamed 'snail fever,' this tropical disease is caused by a parasitic flatworm picked up from freshwater contaminated by infected snails — what is it?
Schistosomiasis: Human disease caused by parasitic worms called schistosomes.
Nicknamed the 'brushwood dog' for its game-flushing hunting style, this is the smallest of Japan's six native dog breeds — which breed?
Shiba Inu: Japanese dog breed. The Shiba Inu (Japanese: 柴犬; Japanese pronunciation: [ɕi.ba.i.nɯ]) is a breed of hunting dog from Japan.
First isolated in 1820 from black nightshade berries, this glycoalkaloid poison also occurs naturally in potatoes as a built-in pest defense. What compound is it?
Solanine: Glycoalkaloid poison found in the nightshade family of plants.
Built from four fused carbon rings, this class of organic compounds includes cholesterol, testosterone, and anabolic performance-enhancers — what is it called?
Steroid: Polycyclic organic compound having sterane as a core structure.
Native to the Balkan Peninsula, this fragrant flowering shrub in the olive family is cultivated widely across Europe and North America for its clusters of purple or white blooms — which species?
Syringa vulgaris: Plant species in the olive family.

This rare chromosomal condition gives affected females four copies of a single chromosome instead of the usual two, and is linked to distinctive facial features and skeletal quirks like incurved pinky fingers — what is it called?
Tetrasomy X: Chromosomal disorder with 4 X chromosomes.
These digits let cats walk in a 'digitigrade' stance, while humans are 'plantigrade,' resting on the soles of their feet instead — what are they?
Nicknamed 'Blinder' by NATO, this disappointing supersonic bomber was still exported to Libya and Iraq, seeing combat against Tanzania and in the Iran–Iraq War — which aircraft?
Tupolev Tu-22: Soviet supersonic heavy bomber.
Native to the wetlands of the Carolinas, this carnivorous plant snaps its jaw-like leaves shut on prey after tiny trigger hairs are touched — which plant?

Venus flytrap: Species of carnivorous plant. It is closely related to the waterwheel plant (Aldrovanda vesiculosa) and the cosmopolitan sundews (Drosera), all of which belong to the family Droseraceae.

In general relativity, this hypothetical region of spacetime is considered the theoretical mirror image of a much better-known cosmic trap — nothing can enter it, though light, matter, and energy may escape. What is this region called?
White hole: Hypothetical object of spacetime. In this sense, it is the opposite of a black hole, from which energy, matter, light and information cannot escape.
First identified in 1789 but not isolated in pure form until much later, this corrosion-resistant, greyish-white transition metal (symbol Zr) closely resembles hafnium and titanium. What element?
Zirconium: Chemical element with atomic number 40 (Zr)
The symbol for meitnerium is Mt. Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.
The symbol for strontium is Sr. Strontium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sr and atomic number 38.

Rosie Huntington-Whiteley: Rosie Alice Huntington-Whiteley (born 18 April 1987) is an English model and actress.

Jane Fonda: Jane Seymour Fonda (born December 21, 1937) is an American actress and activist.

Richard Gere: Richard Tiffany Gere ( GHEER; born August 31, 1949) is an American actor.
In what year was Drew Barrymore born?
Drew Barrymore: Drew Blythe Barrymore (born February 22, 1975) is an American actress, producer, talk show host, and businesswoman.
In what year did Richard Harris die?
Richard Harris: Richard St John Francis Harris (1 October 1930 – 25 October 2002) was an Irish actor and singer.
In what year did Dharmendra die?
Dharmendra (8 December 1935 – 24 November 2025) was an Indian actor, producer and politician, primarily known for his work in Hindi films.
In what year was Army of Thieves first released?
Army of Thieves is a 2021 heist comedy film directed by Matthias Schweighöfer from a screenplay by Shay Hatten, based on a story he wrote with Zack Snyder.
In what year was Oppenheimer first released?
Oppenheimer is a 2023 epic biographical thriller film written, co-produced, and directed by Christopher Nolan.
In what year was The Holdovers first released?
The Holdovers premiered at the 50th Telluride Film Festival on August 31, 2023, and was released in the United States by Focus Features on October 27, 2023.
In what year was Gladiator II first released?
